race: Formula 1 Qatar Airways Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, where Baku is about to get very loud, and the grid is already full of stories.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Russell has pole, Ferrari look sharp, McLaren are pretending this is normal, and Red Bull are quietly smiling at the street circuit.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Let's start with the headlines, because qualifying was not a quiet one, and the start line is already more interesting than the race map.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Russell takes pole in Baku after a dramatic qualifying wall, and Mercedes now have the cleanest seat in the house.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That wall changes the start, and it changes the story, because the front row is now a Mercedes and Ferrari problem on the grid.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Norris says McLaren are miles off pace in Baku practice, so this top ten feels risky, but street circuits love a brave call.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And yes, the race is on Saturday, which is a small twist for a city street circuit, and it makes the whole weekend feel much faster.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Chadwick says driving a Formula One car is top of his bucket list, and after seeing Baku, I think I would say the same thing.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now the big three, because these are the seats we are actually watching, and this is where the race really starts on Saturday.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Russell first. Pole position, best practice, and Mercedes pace that looks honest, which is exactly what you want on a street circuit.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His Baku history helps too. Average finish four point three, best second, and two podiums in three races, so this is not a lucky pole.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But can Ferrari beat him from second, and can Leclerc get the first corner done without a single touch or a single regret?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Leclerc is the man for that job, and he is the one I would trust to make the front row feel genuinely dangerous.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Strong Ferrari, good Baku history, and an average finish of four point seven with two podiums over three races, so this is a proper threat.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a proper front row threat, and if the first sector is tight, Ferrari will be in the mix before the first corner even opens.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Then Piastri in third, because McLaren form is consistent, the grid is kind, and he is the one who can make the midfield look slow.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His Baku record is interesting. Average finish six, best first, and one podium in two races, so he has already shown he can win here.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So if the car recovers, he can be the swing pick, and I would love to see him push Leclerc from the first sector.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I'm not buying a McLaren miracle, but I respect the grid, and I know Baku can flip a weekend with one clean lap.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time, because there is a surprise pick hiding just outside the front group, and I think it is worth a bet.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Lawson starts eleventh, but he has strong Baku history and good pace, so he is my surprise top ten hope if the race gets chaotic.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is a proper gamble, and I like it, because street circuits love a driver who can make a move and hold it through the whole lap.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The penalty list is spicy. Car fourteen takes a thirty place grid penalty, car eighteen takes twenty places, car eleven loses three, and car fifty five loses five.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the kind of chaos that makes Baku fun, and it gives the top ten a little more breathing room for mistakes on the first lap.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And if a Red Bull passes on the first corner, we will all be smiling, because Verstappen is a Baku specialist and can pass.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Hamilton is in sixth, and Norris is in fifth, so the front of the grid is packed with drivers who can make a mistake or a miracle.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is the full top ten in order. Russell, Leclerc, Piastri, Verstappen, Norris, Hamilton, Hadjar, Gasly, Lawson, Colapinto.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Baku, buckle up, because this is the weekend we want, and the first corner is already the best part of the whole race.
